arxiv-2408-10762.title: Sparse Regression for Discovery of Constitutive Models from Oscillatory Shear Measurements
arxiv-2408-10762.creator: Sachin Shanbhag ∗, Gordon Erlebacher
arxiv-2408-10762.description: Abstract We propose sparse regression as an alternative to neural networks for the discovery of parsimonious constitutive models (CMs) from oscillatory shear experiments. Symmetry and frame-invariance are strictly imposed by using tensor basis functions to isolate and describe unknown nonlinear terms in the CMs.

arxiv-2411-11060.title: Patching FPGAs: The Security Implications of Bitstream Modifications
arxiv-2411-11060.creator: Endres Puschner, Maik Ender, Steffen Becker, Christof Paar
arxiv-2411-11060.description: Abstract . FPGA are known for their reprogrammability that allows for post-manufacture circuitry changes. Nowadays, they are integral to a variety of systems including high-security applications such as aerospace and military systems. However, this reprogrammability also introduces significant security challenges, as bitstream manipulation can directly alter hardware circuits.

pmc-11318869.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Simulating biophysically-detailed neuron models is a computationally expensive but effective method for studying local neural circuits. Recent innovations have shown that artificial neural networks (ANNs) can accurately predict the behavior of these detailed models in terms of spikes, electrical potentials, and optical readouts.

The impact of dietary amino acids on metabolic health remains a topic of debate.

pmc-12836584.title: Implementing digital patient-reported outcomes in routine cancer care: barriers and facilitators
pmc-12836584.creator: SG Aanes, S Wiig, C Nieder, EC Haukland
pmc-12836584.description: BackgroundIn cancer care research, there exists a gap between patient-reported outcomes (PROs) and health care personnel-reported outcomes. PROs have shown significant benefits in terms of symptoms, quality of life, reduced hospital admissions and increased overall survival. However, throughout the past decade, PROS have been used mainly in clinical trials and slowly implemented in routine cancer care.

pmc-13136339.title: Identification and clustering analysis of drug-responsive temporally varying genes through high-frequency longitudinal RNA sequencing

pmc-13136339.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). High-frequency longitudinal RNA sequencing has emerged as a powerful approach for capturing dynamic transcriptional responses to therapeutic interventions, yet traditional differential expression analysis fails to identify genes with temporal variability that lack static expression differences. We used our previously developed computational framework for identifying Temporally Varying Genes (TVGs) from daily blood samples collected over 10–21 days in Sprague–Dawley rats treated with hepatotoxic compounds including tetracycline, isoniazid, carbon tetrachloride, and valproate.

pmc-13246078.title: Exploration and optimization of a respiratory outpatient triage model during the X disease epidemic: A retrospective observational study
pmc-13246078.creator: Chao Zhou, Xiao Feng, Hanhan Hong
pmc-13246078.description: Preexamination triage is the critical first line of defense in outpatient settings. During epidemics like the X disease outbreak, traditional models often fail, and inaccurate triage leads to unfavorable patient outcomes and infection risks. This study aims to address the lack of specific, optimized triage workflows for respiratory epidemics. A retrospective observational study was conducted during the “Harmonious Mission-2022” deployment.

pmc-13328666.creator: Filipa Abreu, Nicola Schiel, Antonio Souto, Simone Pika
pmc-13328666.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Conversational turn-taking, the orderly exchange of signals between individuals, is considered an important component of human communication and language. Comparative studies of vocal turn-taking have often been biased toward a limited number of model species and have usually examined only single call types, restricted features of human conversational turn-taking, or captive animals, thereby limiting broader understanding of turn-taking complexity and its evolutionary trajectory.
